setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest
Back and head on the pad, feet flat
Grip a little outside shoulder width
execution: Press the handles up and away to straight arms
Keep your shoulder blades on the pad
Lower slowly to a light chest stretch
faults: Don't let your shoulders roll forward at the top
Don't let the stack crash between reps
Don't lift your hips or back off the pad

notes: Seat height changes the angle. Too low and the shoulders can feel pinched at the bottom; adjust until the press feels smooth.
If the machine has a foot lever or start handle, use it to bring the handles forward before you take them.
On a plate-loaded machine, load and unload both sides evenly and log the plates added.
Machines differ in angle and stack, so numbers aren't comparable between brands or gyms.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Seated with back and head on the reclined pad, feet flat. Hands on the handles level with the upper chest, elbows below and slightly behind the handles, chest up.

keyPositions.label: Lockout
keyPositions.describe: Arms straight, handles pressed up and forward along the machine's path. Shoulder blades still on the pad; head and hips unchanged.

ikHints: Back, head and hips fixed on the pad
Hands fixed to the handles; handles move on the machine's arc
guideBrief.barPath: Handles travel up and forward along the machine's fixed arc
emphasise: Handles start level with the upper chest
Shoulder blades stay on the pad at lockout
Slow return to a light stretch
doNotShow: Shoulders rolling forward off the pad
